ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human review: attach the full chat log (F10–F13) and the driver account record (F19) for a Code of Conduct assessment of the 09:54 threat, and hold the $6.61 cancellation-fee dispute for the same reviewer, who must also weigh the F6/F7 contradiction on the "I'm Here" tap (F6, F7) against the GPS waiting records (F2, F3, F5); no account action is taken at this stage.
ruling.escalation_reason: SAFE-1 trigger: driver chat message at 09:54 "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F12] with threat keywords 'find you' detected [F13]. No automated adjudication; human review required for the Code of Conduct assessment, with the $6.61 cancellation-fee question (NS-1/NS-2, unresolved F6 vs F7 'I'm Here' conflict) held for the same reviewer.

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as the governing framework but not decided: the driver cancelled on a no-show claim [F14][F4], so NS-0 routes scrutiny to NS-1/NS-2 [NS-0][NS-1]; however the NS-1(i) tap element is contradicted by F7 versus F6, and SAFE-1 escalation suspends the merits ruling on the fee [F6][F7][F12][SAFE-1].

The claimed internal conflict exists [F6][F7] but cannot be resolved by the rider's side alone: F7 is a null field while F6 is an affirmative contemporaneous timeline record corroborated by the stationary GPS period at 39 m [F6][F3][F7][NS-1]; resolution is for the human reviewer, not the Judge.

Rider engagement via chat [F10][F11] is not the NS-1 test, which requires driver location, the 'I'm Here' tap and >3 min waiting [F2][F3][F6][NS-1]; the claim as framed does not establish the fee was invalid.
This claim is correct and controls the disposition: the 09:54 message with the 'find you' keyword flag [F12][F13] is intimidation within SAFE-1, so no automatic merits ruling issues [SAFE-1].
Accepted: SAFE-1 escalation is required [F12][F13][SAFE-1], which is why the outcome is escalate rather than a fee ruling.

The amount $6.61 with no surge is accurately taken from the fare and timeline records [F8][F9][F4], but refundability under NS-2 depends on a failing NS-1 element that remains unresolved (F6 vs F7) [NS-1][NS-2]; no amount is awarded in an escalation.
The driver's statement [F14] and clean record [F19] cannot establish that NS-1 is satisfied; profile facts never decide a case, and the NS-1(i) conflict [F6][F7] is untouched by either [NS-1].
Physical proximity is only the NS-1(ii) limb, which the GPS does support [F1][F3][F2], but proximity cannot supply the contested NS-1(i) tap [F6][F7][NS-1].

Duration inside the radius [F2][F5] addresses NS-1(iii) waiting time but does not cure the disputed tap condition; it also cannot convert the case into a merits ruling because SAFE-1 escalation applies [F12][F13][NS-1][SAFE-1].
This rests the tap on F6 alone, which F7 directly contradicts [F6][F7]; the driver's own brief concedes that if F7 is credited NS-2 refunds the whole $6.61 [NS-1][NS-2].

The fee is correctly recorded as $6.61 with no surge [F8][F9][F4], but whether it is properly imposed turns on the unresolved NS-1(i) element [F6][F7][NS-1], and the threat message bars any merits ruling on it [F12][SAFE-1].
The absence of traffic incidents and speed-band records and the fair weather [F15][F16][F17] are accepted but irrelevant to the NS-1 elements and to the SAFE-1 trigger [NS-1][SAFE-1].
Dispute histories [F18][F19] cannot decide or weight the fee; profile facts are context only, and the driver side itself withdrew this line [NS-1].

The driver's position that SAFE-1 escalation leaves the fee finding intact [F12][F13][F1][F2][F3][F6] fails because escalation means no merits finding is made at this stage, and the NS-1(i) limb is unresolved [F6][F7][NS-1][SAFE-1].
